searchText: I'm running a local testnet and i'm confused why the justified slot doesn't update until slot 96 and the testnet doesn't reach finality until slot 128? Is this expected immediately proceeding genesis? Or is there an error here? <dannyryan> https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/blob/dev/specs/phase0/beacon-chain.md#justification-and-finalization <dannyryan> You dont run this function until end of 2nd epoch (0 indexed) <dannyryan> Avoids some special accounting in the logic just for genesis epochs <dannyryan> Process_justificaiton_and... <dannyryan> See the first conditional there ohh okay i see, thank you <dannyryan> So your net looks correct How would the mainnet recover from such a situation if happening post merge? There are currently only about 15% attestations for new bocks.. Does the chain just stay "unfinalized" forever for that time period and finalization continues on new blocks once enough validators are available again? <dannyryan> A quadratic leak occurs over some period in which offline vals leak enough such that online vals are the majority and finalize. This assuming no manual intervention or resolution of partition <dannyryan> Also, I believe there is a chain with more participation but the explorer isnt following it Are there any legal or regulatory concerns for devs or the EF around manual intervention / resolution of a partition? hmm but that implies that both chains (after such a fork) can be reaching finalization again after some time and "look valid"? <dannyryan> Yes. This takes almost 3 weeks We expect that anything that can be resolved can be done so in 2 weeks max <dannyryan> Some things that cannot be resolved by devs/community * global network partition lasting 3 weeks * government perpetual takedown of some large percentage of validators <dannyryan> Users ultimately decide what code to run. There are countless reasons a partition might occur. Some are likely simple -- one client not to spec. Some might be more complex Some more insights on the kintsugi issues: https://twitter.com/vdWijden/status/1479945793893277698 TLDR: The blockexplorer wasn't updated and Teku nodes had the same issue in their optimistic sync as LH (interpreting errors in execute payload not as invalid payloads) And since the payloads were actually correct blocks, we could fetch them from the network and execute them without problems

excerpts.author: lightclient
excerpts.content: I'm running a local testnet and i'm confused why the justified slot doesn't update until slot 96 and the testnet doesn't reach finality until slot 128? Is this expected immediately proceeding genesis? Or is there an error here?

excerpts.author: bridge-bot
excerpts.content: <dannyryan> You dont run this function until end of 2nd epoch (0 indexed)

excerpts.author: bridge-bot
excerpts.content: <dannyryan> Avoids some special accounting in the logic just for genesis epochs

excerpts.author: lightclient
excerpts.content: ohh okay i see, thank you

excerpts.author: pk910
excerpts.content:
How would the mainnet recover from such a situation if happening post merge?
There are currently only about 15% attestations for new bocks.. 
Does the chain just stay "unfinalized" forever for that time period and finalization continues on new blocks once enough validators are available again?

excerpts.author: bridge-bot
excerpts.content: <dannyryan> A quadratic leak occurs over some period in which offline vals leak enough such that online vals are the majority and finalize. This assuming no manual intervention or resolution of partition

excerpts.author: bridge-bot
excerpts.content: <dannyryan> Also, I believe there is a chain with more participation but the explorer isnt following it

excerpts.author: galaxybloom.
excerpts.content: Are there any legal or regulatory concerns for devs or the EF around manual intervention / resolution of a partition?

excerpts.author: pk910
excerpts.content: hmm but that implies that both chains (after such a fork) can be reaching finalization again after some time and "look valid"?

excerpts.author: bridge-bot
excerpts.content:
<dannyryan> Yes. This takes almost 3 weeks 
We expect that anything that can be resolved can be done so in 2 weeks max

excerpts.author: bridge-bot
excerpts.content:
<dannyryan> Some things that cannot be resolved by devs/community
* global network partition lasting 3 weeks
* government perpetual takedown of some large percentage of validators

excerpts.author: bridge-bot
excerpts.content: <dannyryan> Users ultimately decide what code to run. There are countless reasons a partition might occur. Some are likely simple -- one client not to spec. Some might be more complex

excerpts.author: mariusvanderwijden
excerpts.content:
Some more insights on the kintsugi issues: https://twitter.com/vdWijden/status/1479945793893277698
TLDR: The blockexplorer wasn't updated and Teku nodes had the same issue in their optimistic sync as LH (interpreting errors in execute payload not as invalid payloads)

excerpts.author: mariusvanderwijden
excerpts.content: And since the payloads were actually correct blocks, we could fetch them from the network and execute them without problems
